title: Next-Token Prediction and Sampling
summary: A language model outputs a score for every token in its vocabulary. Softmax turns those scores into probabilities, and a sampler (greedy, temperature, top-k, top-p) decides which token is actually written. The same probabilities give you entropy, log-probs and perplexity.
objectives: Turn a vector of logits into probabilities with softmax, with and without temperature
Apply greedy decoding, top-k and top-p (nucleus) filtering to a small distribution by hand
Compute the entropy of a next-token distribution and explain what it says about the model's certainty
Compute log-probabilities and perplexity for a sequence and interpret them
Choose sampler settings for extraction, chat and creative tasks and explain the trade-offs
prerequisites: You should know that a transformer turns a sequence of tokens into one vector per position ([The Transformer Block](/learn/model-foundations/transformer-block)) and what a token is ([Tokenization](/learn/model-foundations/tokenization)). The softmax function was introduced with cross-entropy loss in [How a Network Learns](/learn/model-foundations/how-networks-learn).
